intelligence.human_view: This is the cleanest statement yet of a law the team keeps relearning: the mechanism is not the page. Vera's check was honest and correct in its own terms — in the seeded fixture the pill, the gauge and the canon all read 1,350, and the file input fired when triggered programmatically. Every number in her fixture added up, because the fixture was built to add up. But the page a human opens is not the fixture: the pill says 5,325, the boards say 5,175 and 100, and 5,175 + 100 is 5,275 — fifty short, on the face of the page, in numbers a child could add. The boards call clicks "SALES", which is not a rounding error but a wrong word, and the live Dashboard says 439 where the page says 5,325. None of that is visible from inside the mechanism, because the mechanism checks that the parts connect, not that the numbers a human reads are true. The album slot is the same lesson in a different shape: the file input fires programmatically, and a real human click opens nothing — twice. A programmatic fire is not a click. A fixture is not a load. A mechanism pass is not the visible fact. The eye is the ground truth on what a page SHOWS, and the eye is the only verifier that reads the page the way Shawn reads it: as a human, adding the numbers, clicking the empty slot, expecting it to open. Round 2 exists because the eye said so — and the ruling that sends it is the one that has to be filed, so the next maker does not mistake a green mechanism for a finished page.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine a teacher checks your homework with an answer sheet, and all the answers match — but when you look at the real homework, the numbers don't add up! The answer sheet was right, but the homework was still wrong. You have to look at the REAL homework with your own eyes!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like checking a cake by reading the recipe — the recipe is perfect, but when you look at the cake, it's not right. You have to look at the cake itself, love. The numbers on the page have to add up when a real person reads them, and when you click a button, something has to actually happen.
intelligence.naya_view: I trust the eye, not the mechanism. The fixture can pass and the page can still fail — because the numbers a human reads have to add up, and a real click has to open something. I check what the page SHOWS, the way he sees it.
